input: Draft an emergency financial plan for job loss scenarios

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Whether job loss is already happening vs. a precautionary plan changes the urgency, tone, and immediate actions required.
The plan's coverage — e.g., just cash flow and expenses, or also debt management, investments, insurance, and tax — determines how deep and broad the document needs to be.
A single person with no dependants has a very different financial buffer need and set of obligations than someone supporting a family, which affects every calculation in the plan.
Knowing the current emergency fund size or total liquid savings sets the realistic runway and shapes which strategies are even viable.
The intended format — a spreadsheet, a written document, a checklist — determines how the plan should be structured and delivered.
The target coverage period (e.g., 3 months vs. 12 months of expenses) defines what a 'complete' plan looks like and what financial targets to include.

Whether the plan should prioritise cutting expenses aggressively, protecting investments, or pursuing alternative income streams reflects personal values and risk tolerance, and shapes the recommended actions.

gold.taskTitle: Draft Emergency Financial Plan for Job Loss
gold.taskDescription: Create a personalised emergency financial plan that prepares for or responds to a sudden loss of employment income.

questions.title: Is this plan precautionary or is job loss already happening?
questions.description: Understand whether the user is planning ahead as a precaution or responding to an active or imminent job loss situation.

questions.title: Which financial areas should the plan cover?
questions.description: Determine whether to include only cash flow and monthly expenses, or also debt repayment, investments, insurance, taxes, and government benefits.

questions.title: How many people depend on your income right now?
questions.description: Identify whether the user is planning for themselves alone or for a household with dependants, which changes all financial thresholds in the plan.

questions.title: How much liquid savings do you currently have access to?
questions.description: Establish the existing financial runway so the plan's strategies and urgency levels are grounded in the user's real situation.

questions.title: What format should the finished plan be in?
questions.description: Clarify whether the user wants a written action plan, a checklist, a budget spreadsheet, or a combination of these.

questions.title: How many months of expenses should this plan aim to cover?
questions.description: Set the target survival runway the plan is designed around, such as 3, 6, or 12 months of covered expenses.

questions.title: What is your top priority — cutting costs, protecting assets, or earning alternative income?
questions.description: Understand the user's financial values and risk tolerance so the plan's recommended actions reflect what matters most to them.
